summary: No dip-buying version beat simply holding the NIFTY. Splitting those trades across more companies made results much worse, because each stock adds its own charges.

rows.label: Dip buying, all money in one stock

note: Aug 2017 to Nov 2026, with Groww charges and 0.1% slippage each way. Stocks are today's NIFTY 100, which flatters the trading rules. The NIFTY line is price only, excludes dividends and fund costs, and is past performance rather than a promise.

monthly.note: Don't trust the big numbers. The test used today's NIFTY 100, a list that already contains past winners, so it could choose companies whose success wasn't known at the time. The last 2.8 years are the better warning.
